title: The Shark Diaries
summary: A special Shark Week radio-play episode dramatizing the 1916 Jersey Shore shark attacks, presented as a set of diary entries from the people involved. Josh and Chuck introduce the background: a series of attacks over twelve days in July 1916 at Beach Haven, Spring Lake and other Jersey Shore spots, and then in Matawan Creek, which killed several people and inspired later shark fiction. The hosts introduce the cast, including Dr. John C. Nichols, the ichthyologist who worked with Dr. Frederick Lucas, Charles Van Zandt's sister, and Stanley Fisher and Mary Anderson. The drama follows the attacks, the hunt in Matawan Creek, the hospital recovery of the surviving boy, and closes with Nichols's reflections. The hosts then sign off and credit the production team.

segments.title: Opening banter and background
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the special Shark Week radio-play episode, recap the 1916 Jersey Shore and Matawan Creek attacks, and describe the beach culture of the era. They name the cast and the characters they voice.

segments.title: Diary: Independence Day holiday and the first attack
segments.summary: Diary entries set the scene: a family travels to Beach Haven for the July Fourth holiday. A brother is lost to a shark while swimming far out, and the diary records the response of the victim's family.

segments.title: Diary: Beach Haven attack and Stanley's courtship
segments.summary: Diary entries from Dr. Nichols and from Stanley Fisher's tailor shop cover the second attack in Beach Haven, Nichols's frustration with Lucas, and Stanley's courtship of Mary Anderson.

segments.title: Diary: Spring Lake attack and press conference
segments.summary: Reports of a third attack at Spring Lake, the press conference, and the examination of the Spring Lake victim, Charles Bruder. Nichols doubts Lucas's claim that a shark jaw cannot sever bone. Residents respond with wire netting and armed guards.

segments.title: Diary: Rumors of sharks in the creek and Matawan attacks
segments.summary: Reports reach Matawan of further attacks and kids' conversations about sharks. Nichols mentions an El Nino theory. Then the Matawan Creek attacks begin, and Nichols is dispatched to the town.

segments.title: Diary: Matawan Creek deaths and the shark hunt
segments.summary: Entries describe the deaths of Lester Stillwell and Stanley Fisher in Matawan Creek, the surviving boy Joseph Dunn, the townspeople's shark hunt, and examination of the victims. Nichols considers a great white or tiger shark and notes the captured shark.

segments.title: Diary: Joseph Dunn's hospital recovery and closing reflections
segments.summary: Joseph Dunn recovers in the hospital, and Nichols reflects on the summer of 1916 and the birth of modern ichthyology. Dunn's account is shown in a final diary entry.

segments.title: Credits and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck praise the cast and crew, including Jerry as sound designer, and give listener contact information before the sign-off.
